recommendations.name: South Route
recommendations.summary: Build this page on the trip in from Cascade Pass (the northern half of the high traverse, then back out the same way), and drop the southern Downey Creek approach as the main way in, because the road to that trailhead is closed until at least 2028.
recommendations.detail: Lizard is a side scramble from the White Rock Lakes camp on the Ptarmigan Traverse, so both outings the row describes are real. The deciding fact is that the Suiattle River Road, the only access to the Downey Creek trailhead, is closed at milepost 4 from April 2026 to January 2028, and the trailhead itself is cut off by washouts. Guide services have switched their 2026 trips to an out-and-back from Cascade Pass, or to an exit down the South Cascade River. So the page should start at Cascade Pass (as the itinerary, waypoints 1+ and the north variant already do), return the same way, and mention the Downey Creek route only as the historical southern route that is closed for now. As part of the rewrite, the south-side prose's mislabelled 'South Cascade Glacier to Lizard Col' crossing goes away (that ground is the Dana Glacier / Spire Col side). Also recompute the summit height, which the row gives as both 7,420 and 7,399.

recommendations.name: North Buttress
recommendations.summary: Keep this page on the US-side approach over Hannegan Pass, and rewrite the day plan, times and totals, which currently describe the shorter start from Chilliwack Lake in Canada.
recommendations.detail: Both approaches are documented. Mountain Project lists both the Chilliwack Lake (BC) start (about 9 mi to the 6,480 ft saddle camp) and the Hannegan Pass start (about 17 mi to Bear Creek, then the same climb to the saddle). The Chilliwack Lake start is shorter, but it crosses into the US on foot at an unstaffed border, north of the border its trail has become a bushwhack, and the page cannot promise that crossing is legal. The Hannegan trail is the maintained US route, and the Park Service reports it cleared all the way to Bear Creek. The trailhead card, waypoints, approach prose, primary variant and descent already use Hannegan, so only the Chilliwack-based figures need changing. The whole trip is more like 4-5 days: a documented Hannegan trip to Bear ran about 36 mi and 12,500 ft. The Bear Creek camp has been closed since the 2021 fire, so the day plan must camp elsewhere, for example at Brush Creek, before the climb to the saddle. The Chilliwack Lake start can stay as a secondary variant, with a border caution.

recommendations.name: Direct North Buttress
recommendations.summary: Keep this as its own climb, on the same Hannegan Pass approach as its sister North Buttress page, and replace the distance and elevation totals, which belong to the shorter start in Canada.
recommendations.detail: The Direct North Buttress (Kearney and Knight, 1980; 21 pitches, 5.10-) is a documented line distinct from the 1967 Beckey-Fielding North Buttress. It starts at the toe of the buttress rather than from the glacier couloir, so it is not a duplicate and should not be merged. Its trailhead, road, waypoints and primary variant are all Hannegan Pass, but gain_ft/loss_ft 5,950 and dist_km 14.5 describe the Chilliwack Lake (BC) start. Set them to Hannegan-based round-trip figures that match the sister row once that row is rebuilt: roughly 36-42 mi and 12,000+ ft round trip. The approach prose's '30+ miles and well over 10,000 ft' is already in the right range. The approach prose should also stop giving the West Ridge / Northwest Ridge 'summit goes via' line as if it were this route.

recommendations.name: West Ridge (Beckey Route)
recommendations.summary: Keep this as the West Ridge climb approached from Depot Creek, and rebuild the day plan and times, which describe a boat-and-Perry-Creek trip that belongs to a different route.
recommendations.detail: Mountain Project and multiple trip reports put this route's camp on the 7,200 ft divide at the head of Depot Creek, approached from Chilliwack Lake Road in BC via Depot Creek Falls and Ouzel Lake. That is what the approach, waypoints, variants and descent already say. The itinerary and timing instead describe a Ross Lake water taxi and a Perry Creek bivy at 5,000 ft, and neither appears in any account of this climb. The Little Beaver trail that plan relies on is also currently partly closed. One documented Depot Creek trip for both Mox peaks ran about 24 mi and 11,200 ft over several days, so the day plan should run: to Ouzel Lake, then to the Redoubt col, then summit day via the Col of the Wild, then out. The road block should name Chilliwack Lake Road and the Depot Creek spur (4x4 recommended, locked gate about 0.9 mi up), not Hannegan. The row's internal id says 'se_rib' but its name and content are the West Ridge; the name is correct.

recommendations.name: Cascade-Johannesburg Couloir (East Ridge)
recommendations.summary: Keep this as a one-day climb from the road, since the couloir starts about twenty minutes from the parking lot, and rewrite the day plan that has a six-hour hike to an overnight camp.
recommendations.detail: Two independent trip reports reach the couloir's apron within about 20 minutes of leaving Cascade River Road, and both did the climb as a day trip. The row's approach prose and approach variant already say 'effectively no approach at all'. The itinerary's day 1 (6 h, 3 mi, 3,200 ft up the Cascade Pass trail to a bivy near the col) describes an approach nobody uses: the col is the top of the couloir, not a camp below it. The itinerary should be one alpine-start day from the car, with an optional night at the trailhead. The descent should be the same way back, and the road-gate note (gate at mile 18 in the April-June season) should stay. The timing totals follow from the one-day plan.
